> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release

> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **47** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **172** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **172**: **14** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **56** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **128** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9a0c6ec94b3b56e3517f808c52e6aafca2950cb2` — the merge of head `105ec6c1bc234c47734ab73b7f0736f4160191c6` into base `5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9a0c6ec94b3b56e3517f808c52e6aafca2950cb2 && git checkout 9a0c6ec94b3b56e3517f808c52e6aafca2950cb2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78 105ec6c1bc234c47734ab73b7f0736f4160191c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78 && git merge --no-ff 105ec6c1bc234c47734ab73b7f0736f4160191c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5d4d55aecfb9eabfa7ffd3835a415229a1f50f78` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Clause-② contract review — **PASS** (in-seat, fable tier, epic cloud#1841 PM; reading of PR head 105ec6c1b):

- `AnalyticsResult.fields[].builtinAggregate?: AggregationFunction` (packages/spec/src/contracts/analytics-service.ts) — additive, optional, typed by the EXISTING `AggregationFunction` from `data/query.zod` (the six values `count | sum | avg | min | max | count_distinct`); no second spelling introduced, satisfying ruling B §1.
- Zod mirror in `api/analytics.zod.ts` uses the same `AggregationFunction.optional()` — TS and wire schema agree; spec `check:generated` current per the seat.
- Population rule (service-analytics `queryDataset`): set iff the dataset measure declares `aggregate` and `label == null` — judged on the authored key, never on the resolved string, so an author's label (plain or inline locale map) is never re-labelled; derived measures and dimensions never carry it. This is ruling B §2 exactly.
- Seeds: the built-in dataset seed drops its authored `label: 'Count'` so the seeded measure is a server default again (§2 for the seed site).
- Scope narrowing vs the five named sites (inferMeasure ×2, cube-registry.inferFromObject) accepted on the seat's measured evidence in the PR body: those defaults live on the cube path and do not reach `fields[]`; objectstack#15019 records the dead-code finding. The downstream-contract fixture is a Cube fixture with nothing to mirror; its suite ran green.
- Consumer contract stated in the PR body and already implemented at objectui#7535 (locale lookup keyed on the discriminator, fallback to `label`, then `name`).

Clearing `needs:contract-review` from both carriers. Enqueue after the seat's final CI report.
